summary: Describes how Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) runs over IPv4 and IPv6 when the two systems are a single IP hop apart. It covers how BFD packets are carried so that two directly connected devices can quickly notice when the path between them stops working. It is a Proposed Standard.

eli5.summary: Two kids on either end of a short string keep tugging it. If the tugs stop, both know right away that the string broke.

questions: how does bfd work over ipv4 and ipv6
what is bfd over ipv4 and ipv6
which udp port does bfd use
what is the bfd echo function
subtitle: How two directly connected routers or hosts run fast failure detection over plain IPv4 and IPv6.

tldr.problem: Two systems that are one IP hop apart need a quick way to notice that the path between them has stopped working, and the BFD protocol itself does not say how to carry its packets over IP.
tldr.mechanism: BFD Control packets travel in UDP to destination port 3784 with the TTL or Hop Limit set to 255, one session per interface and protocol, and Echo packets use UDP port 3785.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard and is not obsoleted. It is meant for operator-managed links, not for application-to-application detection across the Internet.

today: RFC 5881 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2010, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on the base protocol in RFC 5880.

sections.title: Why BFD Needs an IP Mapping
sections.content:
Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) tracks connectivity between two systems. This RFC describes the particulars of using BFD to track IPv4 and IPv6 connectivity between systems that are directly connected.

The RFC suggests two uses: supplementing the detection mechanisms in routing protocols, and monitoring router-host connectivity. How BFD interacts with other protocols and system functions is left to the BFD Generic Applications document, RFC 5882. The BFD protocol itself is in RFC 5880.
sections.eli5: BFD is the game of constant tugging on the string. This RFC explains how to play it when the string is a normal Internet link between two neighbors.

sections.title: Applications and Limitations
sections.content:
This use of BFD works for any pair of systems talking IPv4 and/or IPv6 across a single IP hop tied to an incoming interface. That includes physical media, virtual circuits and tunnels.

Each BFD session between two systems MUST use a separate network-layer path in both directions, because demultiplexing depends on it and because several sessions would otherwise protect the same path. If both IPv4 and IPv6 are used on a path, a separate session MUST be set up for each protocol.

The optional Echo function sends packets that the neighbor immediately routes back to the sender. That clashes with ingress filtering, so an implementation that supports Echo MUST make sure ingress filtering is not applied on that interface, or make an exception for Echo packets. It also needs to send packets to its own address, which usually means bypassing the normal forwarding lookup.

BFD is an Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) tool for network-based services. The operator must provision the transmit rates correctly to avoid congestion and false failure detection. It is not applicable to application-to-application failure detection across the Internet, because it cannot detect or avoid congestion; that would need BFD inside a transport with TCP-friendly behavior.
sections.eli5: Only two next-door neighbors can play this game, and each game needs its own string. It is not meant for friends far away across town, because too many tugs could clog the road.

sections.title: Initialization and Demultiplexing
sections.content:
Over a given interface and protocol there is only one BFD session between two systems, and the session is bound to that interface. Because of that, both sides MUST take the Active role, sending their first BFD Control packets with a zero value in the Your Discriminator field.

Any packet from the remote machine with a zero Your Discriminator MUST be matched to the session bound to that remote system, interface and protocol.
sections.eli5: Since each pair of neighbors has only one string, both kids start by saying hello at the same time. Nobody has to wait to be asked.

sections.title: Encapsulation in UDP
sections.content:
BFD Control packets MUST be sent in UDP packets with destination port 3784, inside an IPv4 or IPv6 packet. The source port MUST be in the range 49152 through 65535, and the same source port MUST be used for all Control packets of a session. It SHOULD be unique among all BFD sessions on the system. If more than 16384 sessions are active at once, source ports MAY be reused. A source port can help with demultiplexing, but the mechanisms in RFC 5880 MUST be what finally picks the session.

BFD Echo packets MUST use destination UDP port 3785. Their source port is outside the scope of this RFC. The destination address MUST make the remote system forward the packet back to the sender. The source address MUST be chosen so the remote system does not send ICMP or Neighbor Discovery Redirects. So it SHOULD NOT be in the subnet of the sending interface, and SHOULD NOT be an IPv6 link-local address, unless it is known that the remote system will not send Redirects.

Echo packets MUST be sent so that the remote system actually receives them; on multiaccess media the data-link destination address has to be that of the remote system.
sections.eli5: Each tug is written on a small card with a mailbox number on it. Tugs go to one mailbox number and special bounce-back cards go to another, so the neighbor always knows which kind it got.

sections.title: TTL and Hop Limit Checks, and Security
sections.content:
If BFD authentication is not used, all Control packets MUST be sent with a TTL or Hop Limit of 255, and received Control packets MUST be discarded if the value is not 255. This is the idea described in the Generalized TTL Security Mechanism, RFC 5082: a packet that crossed a router would have a lower value.

If authentication is used, packets are still sent with 255, but the receiver MAY discard packets whose value is not 255. The check MAY be done before cryptographic authentication to avoid unneeded calculation.

The RFC views TTL=255 together with binding to an incoming interface as giving equivalent security to other infrastructure protocols, because it is not trivially spoofable. Using the TTL check together with authentication discards a class of unauthorized packets cheaply, which may help where cryptographic checks are open to denial-of-service attacks. Using or not using the check does not affect interoperability.
sections.eli5: Every tug starts with a secret stamp of 255. A tug from far away would have its stamp worn down on the trip, so the kids can tell it did not come from their neighbor.

sections.title: Addressing Rules
sections.content:
All BFD Control packets MUST travel over the one-hop path that BFD is protecting. On a multiaccess network, they MUST use source and destination addresses from the subnet.

On a point-to-point link, the source address MUST NOT be used to identify the session. The first packet MUST be accepted from any source address, and later packets are matched only by Your Discriminator. This lets the neighbor's source address change. If it does, the local system MUST NOT start sending to the new address; it keeps using the address configured when the session was created. It MAY tell the application that the neighbor's address changed.

The TTL check, or authentication, rules out packets from anyone other than the immediate neighbor.
sections.eli5: The kids recognize each other by the game number, not by street address. If a neighbor moves house, the game goes on, but you keep mailing to the old address until a grown-up says otherwise.

sections.title: BFD Over Tunnels
sections.content:
Many mechanisms tunnel IPv4 and IPv6 over arbitrary topologies. If the tunnel mechanism does not decrement the TTL or Hop Limit of the packet it carries, this RFC's mechanism can detect whether the tunnel is alive.

For tunnels the BFD authentication mechanism SHOULD be used and is strongly encouraged.
sections.eli5: A tunnel is a long hidden pipe that acts like a short string. BFD can tug on it too, and a lock on the pipe is a good idea.
